g.text: What exactly-once means — accuracy and completeness
lost 4 records → 23 · doubled them → 67 · the truth is 45
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
TWO WAYS TO BE WRONG, WITH THE SAME DATA
a correct pipeline is accurate AND complete; losing and duplicating are separate bugs
the truth
9 events, total 45
INCOMPLETE — 4 records lost after a crash
total 23 · 49% low
INACCURATE — the same 4 records applied twice
total 67 · 49% high
exactly-once means neither
each record's contribution appears once, no more and no less
The two failures are symmetric in size here (22 either way) and opposite in sign, which is why one can mask the other in an aggregate.
They have different causes too: completeness fails when a source cannot be replayed, accuracy fails when a replay is not deduplicated.
Step 1/4 — accuracy and completeness are two different failures
Exactly-once is two guarantees, not one. Losing 4 records takes the total to 23; applying the same 4 twice takes it to 67. Both are 49% wrong and
neither is detectable from the number alone — and they are fixed by different mechanisms, at different stages.
What exactly-once means — accuracy and completeness
lost 4 records → 23 · doubled them → 67 · the truth is 45
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
EVERY EVENT, DELIVERED TWICE — WHAT ITS OWN WINDOW READS
A single duplicated record moves its window by between 14% and 100%. The damage is `v` divided by the window's total, so a SMALL window is the
fragile one.
id 8 is the worst case here: 8 → 16. Nothing about that record is special — its window is just thin.
Step 2/4 — one duplicate record, and what it does to a window
The cost of one duplicate is not a fixed percentage — it is `v` over the window's total, so the same retry is a 14% error in one window and a 100%
error in another. That is worth knowing because it means duplicate damage concentrates in the thin windows, which are exactly the ones nobody is
watching.
What exactly-once means — accuracy and completeness
lost 4 records → 23 · doubled them → 67 · the truth is 45
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
WHY DUPLICATES EXIST AT ALL
three ordinary events, each producing a duplicate
a worker crashes mid-batch
the batch is re-sent — its records arrive twice
a send times out but SUCCEEDED
the sender cannot tell, so it retries
a checkpoint commits state but not the offset
the source re-reads from the old offset
the alternative — never retry
every one of those becomes LOST data instead
The last row is why "just do not retry" is not a design. Without retries a timeout becomes a loss, and completeness fails instead of accuracy.
So a distributed pipeline is at-least-once by default, and exactly-once is something built ON TOP of retries, never instead of them.
Step 3/4 — retries are the enemy, and they are not optional
Retries are not a flaw to be removed. A timed-out send that actually succeeded is indistinguishable from one that failed, so the sender must
choose between retrying (risking a duplicate) and not retrying (risking a loss). Exactly-once is the property that makes the first choice safe —
it is built on top of at-least-once, not as an alternative to it.
What exactly-once means — accuracy and completeness
lost 4 records → 23 · doubled them → 67 · the truth is 45
seed: tools/stream_seed.js · total 45 · crash at event 4
TWO SUB-PROBLEMS, VERY DIFFERENT DIFFICULTY
the same guarantee, two completely different mechanisms
per-key STATE — window [12:08, 12:10)
recompute it: SET the total to 8. Idempotent by construction.
an external EFFECT — charge order 4 for 6
cannot be recomputed. The money has moved.
so the problem splits into
dedup records BETWEEN stages, and make the final effect idempotent
and the hard half is the second
the outside world does not support "recompute"
Window state is a deterministic function of the records, so a retry that recomputes it lands on the same value — 8 either way.
A charge is not a function of anything the pipeline holds. Once it has happened, only the external system knows, and the pipeline must ask.
Step 4/4 — and exactly-once STATE is easy; exactly-once EFFECTS are not
This split is the chapter's structure. Making per-key state exactly-once is nearly free: the state is a deterministic function of the records, so
recomputing gives 8 every time. Making an external effect exactly-once is a different problem entirely — the money has moved, nothing in the
pipeline records that, and the only system that knows is the one you are calling.
